churn_resistance.rationale: Upgrades would touch very few files: data access is behind one well-typed module and route args come from typegen. The dings are the hardcoded sprite-URL pattern (against the spec's 'treat the API as a live service'), the unbounded cache, and a duplicated magic constant.

findings.issue: spriteUrl fabricates sprite URLs from the /media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png pattern instead of using the sprites.front_default URL the API data already provides, coupling cards to an undocumented media layout even though the spec says to treat the API as a live service.
findings.suggestion: Use the API-provided sprite URL (e.g. accept the extra fetch for list pages, or cache pokemon records), or at minimum isolate the pattern next to the ApiPokemon sprite types with a comment referencing the documented fallback.

findings.issue: Server-side fetches have no timeout or abort; a stalled PokeAPI request hangs the whole SSR page render.
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) (native in Node 24) and evict the cache entry on abort.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache never removes expired entries — only failed promises are deleted — so a long-running process retains every unique API URL forever.
findings.suggestion: Delete the entry on the expiry check miss, or sweep expired entries when the map grows past a cap.

findings.issue: The alternate-form cutoff (id > 10000) is duplicated between the home loader and cardsFromPokemon as a bare magic number.
findings.suggestion: Export a named MAX_SPECIES_ID constant from lib/api.server.ts and use it in both places.

findings.issue: idFromUrl regex-parses API URLs instead of using the URL platform API.
findings.suggestion: Parse with new URL(url).pathname.split('/') and take the last numeric segment; more robust to trailing-slash variants.

findings.issue: Leftover template comment ('// Config options... // Server-side render by default...') with no informational value.
findings.suggestion: Remove it or replace with a note about the actual choices (SSR + default entry server).

summary: This app is fully on React Router's current stable release (8.5) with v8-era conventions — +types route modules, root Layout/ErrorBoundary, data() 404 throws, Vite 8 native tsconfig paths — and a lean dependency set that matches the official template. Data access is isolated behind a single well-typed module, so both framework and API changes would touch few files. What keeps it from exemplary is a handful of small robustness gaps: a hardcoded sprite-URL pattern, no fetch timeout, an unbounded cache, and duplicated magic numbers.
